findings.title: Ratchet Check 3 uses line-split regex instead of @typescript-eslint/parser (design spec deviation)
findings.rationale: design.md D4 and tasks.md T-17 explicitly require @typescript-eslint/parser for AST-based ImportDeclaration analysis. The implementation uses comment-stripped newline-split text search. A multi-line import whose `from "command-registry"` clause is on a different line from the `import {` keyword would silently evade the check, defeating the ratchet for that pattern. The design requirement states: 'AST 等の構造検査を優先し、コメントや文字列で誤検知する単純 grep だけに依存しないこと'.

findings.title: Uses ctx!.invokerCwd instead of process.cwd() as specified in tasks.md T-14 and TC-023
findings.rationale: tasks.md T-14 and test-case TC-023 specify process.cwd() as the CWD argument for executeRulesNew and executeReviewersNew. The original inline handlers in command-registry.ts (main branch) used process.cwd(). The extracted handlers use ctx!.invokerCwd. usage-handler.ts has the same substitution. The requirement '意味を変えずに移動する' (move without changing meaning) is technically violated. In practice ctx.invokerCwd equals process.cwd() at dispatch time, making the substitution functionally equivalent but undocumented. TC-023 asserts process.cwd() is used, but no automated test verifies the argument value.

findings.title: Duck-type error guards added outside R3a scope (pure code movement constraint)

The duck-type guards accept any Error with a matching .name (and exitCode property for SpecRunnerError), which is semantically broader than instanceof. This is outside the declared scope and is a minor behavior change in edge cases (e.g. an Error from an unrelated module with name === 'FlagParseError').

findings.rationale: Check 3 splits the source by newline and looks for lines starting with 'import' that contain 'command-registry'. findings.title: Ratchet Check 1 misses named inline function expressions
findings.rationale: Check 1 detects inline handlers via `spec.handler.name === "handler"`, which catches anonymous arrow/function expressions (V8 infers the property name). However, a named inline function expression like `handler: async function myFn() {}` has `.name === "myFn"` and passes the check undetected, even though the implementation is still embedded inline in the registry literal.

findings.title: findValueImportsFrom silently passes unparseable files in Check 3
findings.rationale: The catch block in `findValueImportsFrom` returns an empty array when `@typescript-eslint/parser` fails to parse a file. If a `src/cli/*.ts` file contains syntax that the installed parser version cannot handle, any value import from `command-registry` in that file would be silently missed by Check 3.

observations.title: handleRequestLs and handleRequestPrompt have zero-parameter signatures
observations.rationale: Both functions omit `parsed` and `ctx` parameters. TypeScript allows this since `CommandHandler` is `(parsed, ctx?) => Promise<void>` and callbacks may have fewer parameters than the target type. The functions are called as `await spec.handler!(parsed, ctx)` in bin/specrunner.ts with arguments silently ignored. No correctness impact; consistent with original inline handlers.

findings.rationale: Finding [3] (d581ef8e) claims T-14 and TC-023 require process.cwd(); iter-6 regression gate reported it "FIXED" when code used process.cwd(). The current code uses ctx!.invokerCwd, matching finding [8] (7bdae8c0). However, tasks.md T-14 (lines 252-254) and test-cases.md TC-023 (lines 322-324) both explicitly require ctx!.invokerCwd, not process.cwd(). Finding [3]'s premise is factually wrong about the spec. Fixing [3] (switching to process.cwd()) would violate [8] and the spec; keeping the current state leaves [3] technically "regressed" from the iter-6 perspective. Operator must decide: accept ctx!.invokerCwd as correct (satisfies T-14, TC-023, finding [8]) and retire finding [3] d581ef8e as superseded, or provide authoritative ruling on which value to use.

options.label: Accept ctx!.invokerCwd (retire finding [3] d581ef8e)
options.consequence: Current code is kept as-is; finding [3] is closed as superseded by corrected spec (T-14, TC-023, finding [8]). Finding [8] (7bdae8c0) is satisfied.

options.label: Revert to process.cwd() (retire finding [8] 7bdae8c0)
options.consequence: Code switches back to process.cwd() in scaffold-handlers.ts; this fixes finding [3] but re-introduces finding [8] and contradicts tasks.md T-14 and TC-023.

findings.title: process.exit count scenario fails; normative MUST is satisfied
findings.rationale: The spec scenario for 'repository 全体の process.exit 件数が変化しない' uses `grep -r 'process.exit' src/ --include='*.ts' | wc -l`. Base = 104; HEAD = 131 (+27). Production-only (excluding tests) went 95→98 (+3) due to JSDoc comment lines added to handler functions (credentials.ts, init.ts, login.ts). All 67 real code process.exit calls were moved 1:1 from registry to handlers — the normative MUST ('集約・削減・return contract 化を行わない') is satisfied. The scenario command is too broad (counts comment lines and test file references added by other required changes).

options.label: Update spec scenario grep command
options.consequence: Amend spec.md scenario to exclude comment lines and test files: `grep -r 'process\.exit' src/ --include='*.ts' | grep -v '\.test\.\|__tests__\|^\s*\*\|^\s*//' | wc -l`. Measurement then matches (95→95 real code, ignoring comment+test additions). spec-fixer resolves.

options.label: Remove JSDoc comment lines about process.exit from handler files
options.consequence: Delete the 3 JSDoc `*` comment lines in credentials.ts, init.ts, login.ts that mention process.exit. Reduces doc quality but makes the production count strictly 95→95. code-fixer resolves.
